pr.title: feat(local): model-free duplicate-work guards for declarations
pr.body:
### Motivation

Issue #576 calls for checks that avoid duplicate proof work and overlapping
worker assignments. This PR implements parts A, B and C. Part D, the documented
just-in-time update and approval-carry workflow, remains open.

### Description

- Add a model-free Lean declaration scanner and `local/bin/dup_check.py` for
  matching declaration names, normalized statements, blueprint labels and
  branch contributions against a local Git reference. Matches are advisory
  prompts for mathematical inspection. Exit 0 means no match, 3 means matches,
  4 means the reference could not be read and the check was skipped, and 2
  means a usage or environment error.
- Add an append-only declaration-claims registry and a repository copy of the
  atomic worker-claim script. Declaration claims and worker reservations remain
  distinct records.
- Add an advisory pre-dispatch check and document duplicate-work checks in
  section 7 of the issue/PR protocol. Existing section 6 remains unchanged.
- Include a dated sweep of 69 open PRs: 38 have declarations matched on main,
  including 34 with fully qualified name matches. The report distinguishes
  matched declarations from match counts and documents stale-stack limits.
- Reuse the existing Lean parser through an optional text input. No Lean
  statement, blueprint completeness claim or merge gate changes.

### Testing

- All nine exact-head local CI contexts succeeded on `d418467d`.
- The fresh independent reviewer ran all 55 tests in the four new test
  modules successfully using synthetic repositories, with no network or model
  calls and a clean worktree before and after.
- The reviewer checked the missing-reference exit-4 behavior, existing
  duplicate exit-3 behavior, protocol numbering, sweep counts and front matter.
  The sweep was checked for internal consistency and one sampled match; the
  reviewer did not rerun the full sweep or full test suite.

---
Addresses #576

# Review - PR 579 @ d418467d6b0b9c786284b6639f22fea8a20f9e0d

Independent review by a Claude Opus helper (owner-authorized 2026-09-17); no author, fixer or prior reviewer context reused. Trusted prompt, persona and policy ref: cbb95dc49eebf388180e51d4c46c6b656d63e936. Workflow-layer and documentation change only: 14 files, 2684 insertions / 3 deletions against merge base 7c3f512e (base branch `main`), adding a model-free duplicate-declaration scanner, its CLI and claims registry, a dispatch-time guard, a repository copy of the worker-claim script, protocol prose and one generated sweep report; no Lean statement, definition, blueprint node or gate is touched.

## Findings

- none

## Review

Scope and policy. Trusted policy was read from `github/main` at cbb95dc4 (`local/personas/reviewer.md`, `local/personas/prose-reviewer.md`, `local/protocols/review.md`, `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` section 5, and the proof-integrity and faithful-statement sections of `AGENTS.md`); nothing was read from the branch as policy. The published head d418467d equals the worktree HEAD. Exact-head CI is green: `local-ci/summary` success, with build, blueprint-render, blueprint-sync, paper-gaps, file-length, proof-debt, proof-evasion and statement-origin all success. The branch carries three commits: the feature commit, a merge of current `github/main`, and the review-fix commit; the main-relative diff is the 14 files above.

Proof integrity. `git diff --name-only` against the merge base lists zero `.lean` files and no blueprint TeX, no gate script and no CI configuration; the only `axiom` token added anywhere in the diff is inside the declaration-head regex of `scripts/dup_scan.py`, and no `sorry`, `admit` or `native_decide` appears. The single change to an existing module is the keyword-only `text=` parameter on `scripts/blueprint_lean_sync.collect_file_lean_decls` (default `None`, previous body preserved); I checked every caller in the repository (`blueprint_lean_sync.py:480,924`, `check_source_statement_changes.py:125`, `scripts/tests/test_blueprint_lean_sync.py:373`) and none passes it, so the blueprint-sync and statement-origin gates are unaffected — their green steps at this head agree. Nothing in the new tooling can weaken a statement: it reads blobs with `git show` and prints names. `local/bin/claim.sh` is a faithful copy of the operator script it names; I diffed it against `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/owner-bin/qpbt-claim.sh` and the only changes are the comment header, the `MIPSTARRE_CLAIM_FILE`/`MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT` indirection, an added `mkdir -p` and the usage string — the awk claim/release semantics, the flock and the on-disk line format are byte-identical.

Prior review. The earlier marked review 5237652764 (head e1f09d31) left four unchecked findings; I re-checked each against this head rather than trusting the fix commit. F1: `_matches_on_ref` no longer short-circuits silently — a new `_unreadable_ref` is consulted first by `check`, `sweep`, `claim`, `claims-check` and `predispatch`. Verified by running the tool in the PR worktree: `claims-check --ref no-such-ref` prints "ref no-such-ref not present locally; duplicate check skipped (this tool never fetches on its own)" and exits 4, the same query against `github/main` still exits 3 with the `file:line`, and `check --ref no-such-ref --json` returns a `skipped` key with exit 4; the "no duplicate" line is no longer printed for an unread ref, and the docstring at `local/bin/dup_check.py:27-33` now states the rule. F2: the headings of `local/protocols/issues-prs.md` now ascend 1-7 (`## 7. Duplicate-work guards` at :306, after `## 6. Owner inbox…` at :257), and no existing section was renumbered, so the four files citing "section 6" still point at the owner-inbox section. F3: the per-PR table now has separate "already on the reference" (distinct matched declarations, new helper `matched_declarations` at `scripts/dup_scan.py:367`) and "matches" columns with a note above the table; no row of the regenerated report exceeds its new-declarations column (#398 reads 200/200/222, #400 reads 7/7/26). F4: the front matter reads `pr: "#579"`.

Code. The scanner reuses `blueprint_lean_sync`'s Lean parser and `strip_lean_comments_preserve_lines` instead of writing a second one, and sits beside `scripts/check_duplicate_private_helpers.py`, the existing textual declaration audit; I found no declaration-index helper on `main` that it duplicates. The synthetic-anchor trick in `decls_from_text` is sound (`collect_file_lean_decls` derives `rel` as `lean_file.relative_to(lean_root.parent)`, and `/dup-scan/<rel>` against `/dup-scan/root` yields `<rel>`), and the `TypeError` guard gives a clear message against an un-upgraded helper. `new_declarations` feeds an already-computed merge base into a `base...head` diff, which is the same commit set. In `dispatch.sh` the guard sits after `die`/`note` (:76,:83), `ISSUE` (:162) and `SCRIPT_DIR`/`REPO_ROOT` (:271-272); the mode word is validated with `die 2`, a missing `dup_check.py`, a non-numeric scope word, exit 4 and any unexpected exit only warn, and only `fatal` plus exit 3 refuses — so the guard cannot silently stop a dispatch, and `DUP_OUT="$(…)" && DUP_RC=0 || DUP_RC=$?` records the real exit code under `set -e`. I ran the four new test modules in the PR worktree with byte-code writing disabled: 55 tests, all passing, fixtures synthetic (temp git repositories, a stub `codex` on PATH, no network, no model), and `git status --porcelain` in the worktree was empty before and after. Two non-blocking observations, neither contradicting the documented behaviour: `predispatch` checks the issue's claimed names only against the ref, not against other issues' open claims, so a claim recorded with `--force` over another issue's claim is re-warned at dispatch only if `main` also has the name (the cross-issue refusal happens at claim time, which is what `issues-prs.md` section 7 describes); and `read_claims` uses `path.read_text()` with the locale default while `append_claim` writes `encoding="utf-8"`.

Prose. The sweep report follows the dated-filename rule and the audit metadata format, its headline (69 examined, 38 flagged, 34 by fully qualified name) matches the 69 table rows, the detail cap arithmetic is right ("and 210 more" for 222 matches with 12 shown), and the Limitations section states the three real caveats plus the skipped-head rule. I independently confirmed one sampled match, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus.stateQForm_zero`, at `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:43` on `github/main`. Section 7 of `issues-prs.md` and the registry README describe the implemented behaviour, including advisory exit 4, `--force` semantics and the separation between declaration claims and worker claims; the `EVOLUTION.md` entry has the Trigger/Change/Expected-effect fields of `local/protocols/meta.md`, and its trigger — the owner decision recorded in issue #576, itself logged in `results/telemetry/events.md` on 2026-09-17 — is one of the triggers standing principle 2 allows, so the protocol amendment is evidence-driven. PR body and commit conventions hold: `type(scope): short description` subjects, Motivation/Description/Testing, and no closing keyword bound to a number in the commit messages.

Not checked. I did not run `lake build`, the pre-commit hook, `ci.sh` or the full test suite (only the four new modules), and no Lean file needed elaboration because none changed. I did not re-run the sweep, so its per-PR counts are checked only for internal consistency and one sampled match. I did not exercise the GitHub reads of `sweep` or `check --pr`, `predispatch` inside a real dispatch against the live registry, or the `--node` blueprint-label path. The committed registry file is empty at this head, so its conflict logic is covered by the unit tests only.

VERDICT: APPROVED (code=APPROVED, prose=APPROVED)

# Review - PR 579 @ e1f09d319413c152ed9d3a0e49f8535cafa4747a

Independent review by a Claude Opus helper (owner-authorized 2026-09-17); no author, fixer or prior reviewer context reused. ## Findings

- [ ] F1 (code; changes) local/bin/dup_check.py:178 - `_matches_on_ref` returns an empty list when `ref_exists(repo, ref)` is false, so `claim` and `claims-check` report a clean result for a reference they never read. Verified at this head in the PR worktree: `dup_check.py claims-check --issue 999999 --name MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus.stateQForm_zero --ref no-such-ref` prints `no duplicate of 1 name(s)/declaration(s) on no-such-ref` and exits 0, while the same name against `github/main` correctly exits 3. This contradicts the module's own exit-code contract at local/bin/dup_check.py:28-29 ("`4` advisory - ... the ref is absent locally, so nothing could be checked"), which only `cmd_predispatch` (:357) implements, and it silently defeats the guard in exactly the case it is meant to cover: in any checkout without a `github` remote the default `--ref github/main` is absent, so `claim` records the claim and prints "no duplicate" for every name. Fix: in `_matches_on_ref`, or in `cmd_claim`/`cmd_claims_check` before calling it, treat an absent ref as unchecked - either raise through `_require_ref` (exit 2) or return exit 4 with the "ref not present locally; duplicate check skipped" wording `cmd_predispatch` already uses, and do not print the "no duplicate" line in that case.
- [ ] F2 (prose; changes) local/protocols/issues-prs.md:252 - the new "## 7. Duplicate-work guards" is inserted before "## 6. Owner inbox and mathematical-gap escalation", which this head still carries at :315, so the document now runs 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 6. Four files direct readers to a numbered section of this protocol (local/personas/mathfix.md:5 and :20, local/personas/main.md:16, local/personas/orchestrator.md:32, local/protocols/sessions.md:223 all cite "section 6"), so out-of-order numbering is a navigation defect in a file agents read at session start. Fix: move the new section below the owner-inbox section and keep it numbered 7, or renumber so the headings ascend.
- [ ] F3 (prose; minor) audits/2026-09-17_superseded-pr-sweep.md:53 - the per-PR table column "already on the reference" holds `len(row["duplicates"])`, a count of matches, not of declarations, so it exceeds the "new declarations" column whenever one declaration matches several ways: PR #398 reads 200 new against 222 "already on the reference" (:55), and PR #400 reads 7 against 26 (:63). As written the row is arithmetically impossible and invites the reader to overstate the overlap. The generator is scripts/dup_scan.py:486. Fix: retitle the column "matches on the reference" in `render_sweep_markdown`'s header row and regenerate the report, or count distinct matched declarations there instead.
- [ ] F4 (prose; minor) audits/2026-09-17_superseded-pr-sweep.md:9 - the front matter carries `pr: ""` although the audit is tied to this pull request; audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md (Metadata) says to use `pr: "#M"` when the audit belongs to a pull request, and the generator already accepts `--pr`. Fix: regenerate with `--pr 579` or set the field to `pr: "#579"`.

## Review

Checked. Trusted policy was read from `github/main` at bff096a9 (`local/personas/reviewer.md`, `local/personas/prose-reviewer.md`, `local/protocols/review.md`, `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` section 5, the proof-integrity and faithful-statement sections of `AGENTS.md`); the personas were never read from the branch. Exact-head CI is green: `local-ci/summary` success with build, blueprint-render, blueprint-sync, paper-gaps, file-length, proof-debt, proof-evasion and statement-origin all success at this head. No earlier marked review exists on this PR, so nothing prior had to be re-checked.

Proof integrity. The diff touches no `.lean` file, no blueprint TeX and no gate script: `git diff --stat` against the merge base lists only `audits/`, `local/bin/`, `local/protocols/`, `local/registry/`, `scripts/` and `scripts/tests/`. The only change to an existing Python module is the optional `text=` parameter on `scripts/blueprint_lean_sync.collect_file_lean_decls` (default `None`, previous body preserved), and its other caller at `collect_lean_decls` is unchanged, so blueprint-sync behaviour is untouched - the green blueprint-sync step agrees. No `sorry`, `axiom`, `native_decide` or statement edit appears anywhere in the diff, and nothing in the new tooling can weaken a statement: it only reads blobs and prints names. `local/bin/claim.sh` is a faithful copy of the operator script it names - I diffed it against `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/owner-bin/qpbt-claim.sh` and the only changes are the comment header, the `MIPSTARRE_CLAIM_FILE`/`MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT` indirection, an added `mkdir -p` and the usage string; the awk claim/release semantics and the on-disk line format are byte-identical.

Reuse and correctness. The scanner reuses `blueprint_lean_sync`'s Lean parser and `strip_lean_comments_preserve_lines` rather than writing a second one, and it sits beside `scripts/check_duplicate_private_helpers.py`, which is the existing textual declaration audit; I found no pre-existing declaration-index helper on `main` that this duplicates. The synthetic-anchor trick in `decls_from_text` (scripts/dup_scan.py:218-224) is sound: `collect_file_lean_decls` derives its relative path as `lean_file.relative_to(lean_root.parent)`, and with `lean_file = /dup-scan/<rel>` and `lean_root = /dup-scan/root` that yields `<rel>` exactly. `new_declarations` passes an already-computed merge base into a `base...head` diff, which is the same commit set because the merge base is an ancestor. In `dispatch.sh` the new block sits after `die`/`note` (:76, :83), `ISSUE` (:161) and `SCRIPT_DIR`/`REPO_ROOT` (:271-272) are set, the mode word is validated, and every non-`fatal` path only warns, so the guard cannot silently refuse a dispatch. I ran the four new test modules in the PR worktree with byte-code writing disabled: 48 tests, all passing in 3.1s, worktree left clean. The tests cover an absent *branch* ref for `check` but not the absent-ref path of `claim`/`claims-check`, which is how F1 survived.

Prose. The sweep report follows the dated-filename rule and carries YAML front matter with quoted `issue`; its Limitations section states the three real caveats (textual matching, stack staleness against a merged parent, blindness to overlap between two open PRs) and the method section is accurate against the code it names. Its headline counts are internally consistent with the table (38 flagged, 34 of them by fully qualified name), and the absence of PR #579 itself with 69 rows against 70 open PRs today is consistent with a report generated before this PR existed. I spot-checked one claimed match, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus.stateQForm_zero`, and it is indeed declared on `github/main` at `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/LinePointOverlap.lean:43`. The protocol prose in `issues-prs.md` section 7 and the `EVOLUTION.md` entry describe the implemented behaviour, including the advisory exits, `--force` semantics and the separation between declaration claims and worker claims; the only prose defects I found are F2, F3 and F4. Commit conventions hold: `feat(local): ...` subject, 55 characters, Motivation/Description/Testing in the PR body, and the commit message uses "Addresses" rather than a closing reference.

Not checked. I did not run `lake build`, the pre-commit hook, `ci.sh` or the full 733-test suite (the four new modules only), and no Lean file needed elaboration because none changed. I did not re-run the sweep, so the per-PR counts in the report are checked only for internal consistency and one sampled match, not reproduced. I did not exercise `sweep`'s or `check --pr`'s GitHub read, `predispatch` inside a real `dispatch.sh` run, or the `--node` blueprint-label path. The claims registry file is empty at this head, so its conflict logic is covered only by the unit tests.

VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED (code=CHANGES_REQUESTED, prose=CHANGES_REQUESTED)
